# Alloy Studio workflow plan

Alloy Studio will open a Blueprint-style workflow canvas for designing an alloy, running individual calculations, and inspecting what each calculation needs. A user should be able to run an Al–Cu equilibrium calculation, open its phase table, discover which phase is holding up a density estimate, supply a reference for that phase, and rerun Density using the saved equilibrium result.

This document specifies planned behavior. The node library and field definitions are in the [node catalog](alloy-studio-node-catalog.md). Current equilibrium, transport, and property behavior is documented in [processing methods](processing.md).

## Entry points and starter workflow

- Put **Alloy Studio** in the far-left featured menu tile, **Phase Diagrams** second, and **Settings** after the scientific workspaces. Keep the crystal transition shared by the main menu and scientific screens.
- Open the last project or show **Blank Workflow**, **Al–Cu Equilibrium**, and **Open Workflow** when there is no recent project. The starter opens directly into an editable graph with named inputs, visible wires, and a fit-to-graph view.
- Replace the Create Alloy and Optimize Alloy wizard entries when the starter covers the existing phase calculation and inspection workflow. Put optimization back in the template list once it can execute valid objectives and constraints. Hide the separate Mechanical Properties menu entry. Expose measured test data and supported property methods through workflow nodes as they are integrated.
- Use **Al balance, 4 wt% Cu**, the bundled Al assessment, **101325 Pa**, **298.15 K** initial and cooling target, **1873.15 K** melt, and **21** equilibrium cooling points as editable starter inputs. Supply a separate **Equilibrium at Point** node for a user who wants to calculate one state without a thermal schedule.
- Include **Tracer Diffusivity** in the starter. Its initial selection uses the supported dominant solution phase and exposes the selected phase and actual calculation temperature.
- Show partial property coverage on the Density node if a phase lacks compatible density data. Let the user inspect that phase and optionally add **Resolve Phases** or **Attach Reference** on the density branch. Keep the final Phase Set available to the viewer and transport branch.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C["Composition · Al–4 wt% Cu"] --> E["Equilibrium Along Schedule"]
    S["Processing Schedule"] --> E
    A["MatCalc Al"] -->|Assessment| E
    A -->|Assessment and Physical Data| D["Density"]
    A -->|Assessment and Mobility Data| T["Tracer Diffusivity"]
    E -->|Final Phase Set| V["Phase Viewer"]
    E -->|Final Phase Set| D
    E -->|Final Phase Set| T
```

## Workspace layout

| Region | Default | Contents and actions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Top bar | Visible | Project name, save state, undo/redo, **Fit Graph**, **Run Graph**, and panel toggles. Keep the existing shell Back and Settings actions reachable. |
| Canvas | Fills remaining space | Pan, zoom around the pointer or touch midpoint, drag nodes by the header, box-select, and arrange nodes. A user can expand a node to see optional pins or collapse it to the header and connected pins. Drag a file here to import a reusable input. |
| Left project drawer | Closed | Workflows, imported files, saved Phase Sets, and named Material States. Search by name or document kind. Drag a saved item into the graph to create a typed source node. |
| Right Inspector | Open on desktop | Selected node's settings, connected inputs, latest results, coverage, and provenance. Selecting a pin or wire shows both endpoints, type, shape, units where applicable, current artifact, and stale status. Keep the current selection when the drawer closes. |
| Bottom run bar and drawer | Status strip visible, drawer closed | Run state, counted progress where available, and Cancel. Open the drawer for per-node run history, warnings, errors, and elapsed time. Selecting an issue centers and focuses the corresponding node or pin. |
| Preview | Selected in Inspector or pinned to canvas backdrop | Inspect a phase table, chart, microstructure, image, or text output. **Use as Backdrop** pins a single image-capable preview beneath the grid and wires. Show a dimming control so the graph stays readable. |

At widths below 1100 CSS px, let the project drawer overlay the canvas and keep the Inspector collapsible. Below 760 CSS px, open the Inspector and run log as bottom sheets with one sheet visible at a time. Keep a keyboard-accessible node list and **Connect To** action as alternatives to canvas gestures. With touch, a long press on empty canvas opens Add Node. Keep touch targets at least 44 by 44 CSS px and let scrolling work outside the graph. Use the same node and pin names in the canvas and Inspector.

### Visual direction

Use the supplied Unreal Engine Blueprint screenshot as the reference for node anatomy. Its strongest details are raised and bevelled category headers, dark pin rows beneath the header, hollow and filled pins, curved wires that visibly branch, compact inline values, and small utility nodes such as the equality operator. Bring those details into Rutile's existing crystal scene, smoked glass buttons, bright edge highlights, and dark theme.

- Begin with a near-black canvas around `#0B1017`, a fine grid every **20 px** at 100% zoom, and a slightly brighter major line every fifth interval. Fade minor lines as the graph zooms out. Let the crystal show softly behind the grid during entry and settle to a static, low-opacity backdrop during editing.
- Use **14–16 px** corners, a clipped glass gradient, a **1 px** inner top highlight, a thin rim, and a soft cast shadow on node bodies. Use slightly translucent tinted bodies for connected nodes and stronger opacity at text and controls. Keep live backdrop blur on bounded surfaces such as the toolbar, drawers, and node menu. Simulate the node glass with layered gradients so large graphs can pan without per-node blur.
- Use category colors on glossy headers. Inputs and sources use blue, equilibrium and processing use teal, reference and conversion nodes use violet, properties use green, and viewers use slate. Wires and pins keep the data-family colors from the [node catalog](alloy-studio-node-catalog.md#pin-shape-and-color). Keep names and icons visible when colors are hard to distinguish.
- On a fully disconnected node, reduce the saturation of its header and dim the body and shadow. Keep pin and title labels readable. A source with an output connection or a terminal viewer with an input connection counts as connected. Required missing inputs get a hollow pin plus an issue message. Optional unwired pins stay neutral.
- Draw ordinary wires as cubic curves with roughly **2 px** strokes at 100% zoom. Give the stroke a wider invisible hit target. Use a distinct focus outline for the selected node, a stronger wire accent for the selected connection, and optional upstream/downstream highlights when inspecting a branch. Use filled pins for connections and hollow pins for available connections.
- Show short labels and compact inline values on the body. Composition basis, temperature, pressure, and defaults stay visible when they affect interpretation. Put full source hashes, model settings, and failure details in the Inspector. Put **▶** on the top right of a runnable node, with focus text such as **Run Density**.

### Motion and rendering

| Trigger | Planned motion | Settled or reduced-motion behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enter Alloy Studio | Reuse the shell crystal dive. Bring in the grid and workspace as the camera settles, then reveal the default view of the graph. | Use the existing wide lattice cache during the dive and rebuild settled visible layers at the view's device pixel scale. Show the workspace immediately in reduced motion. |
| Add a node or establish a connection | Use a short **120–180 ms** rise and settle on placement, with a brief edge highlight and a wire draw toward the receiving pin. | Place the node and completed wire immediately when reduced motion is enabled. |
| Hover or focus a node | Let a restrained highlight travel across the header bevel. Lift the shadow subtly. | Keep the focus outline, with static gloss in reduced motion. |
| Open or close a drawer | Slide the glass surface and fade it over **160–220 ms**. Preserve the project camera position and keep the selected node visible. | Show the final layout immediately in reduced motion. |
| Run a node | Animate a small edge or header fill driven by real progress. Use a static pending state for stages with no known count. A completed output can briefly accent the downstream wire. | Always show the stage and real counts when known. Keep pending, complete, and error states readable with motion disabled. |

Reuse the shared shell appearance and motion preferences. Use HTML for node controls and SVG for the first wire layer. Keep world coordinates separate from screen transforms so pan and zoom move the grid, nodes, and wires together. Coalesce geometry updates during drags with `requestAnimationFrame` and redraw only the affected wires when their endpoints change. Raster previews rebuild at the settled display scale. Use browser checks at DPR 1 and 2, with both motion settings. [Current shell and lattice behavior](ui-ux.md)

## Building and running a graph

1. **Add a node.** Right-click empty canvas to open the menu at the pointer with the search field focused. Typing filters labels, categories, and aliases such as “Young's modulus.” Arrow keys and Enter place the selection. Escape closes the menu. Dragging a wire into open space opens the same menu filtered by the originating pin. If the user picks a node, place it and connect the matching pin. Prefer exact matches, then show the available conversion beside each other candidate. Offer a pin picker when the selected node has multiple equally suitable pins.
2. **Connect typed inputs.** Connect one output to any number of compatible inputs. For multiple items, use a collection pin or an explicit Assemble node. Validate kind, shape, quantity, and required basis both when editing and before a run. Keep conversion nodes visible and included in undo/redo. Insert **Solid Fill** automatically for Color → Image. For Material Color → Image, offer **Phase Swatches**, **Select Phase Color**, and **Blend by Visible Area**. Enable the blend only with exposed-area information, compatible lighting, and coverage for the selected phases. Show the missing input when a wire cannot connect.
3. **Edit and inspect.** Inline controls handle common values and the Inspector handles source assignment and model settings. Dragging a wire temporarily highlights compatible targets. Support disconnect, reroute, undo/redo, and keyboard connection. Keep view position, selection, panel state, and style changes out of scientific inputs.
4. **Run to a node.** A node's **▶** runs that node and any missing or stale prerequisites, then stops. Reuse matching upstream results. **Run Graph** evaluates the enabled terminal branches and their dependencies. Viewers refresh on completed inputs. A blocked branch leaves independent branches runnable.
5. **Explain status in place.** Use Draft for a newly placed node, Ready when required inputs exist, Queued and Running during work, Completed for a current result, Stale for a result from earlier inputs, and Canceled or Failed for terminated work. Use **Needs data** for missing prerequisites and **Unavailable** when a calculation runs but its method lacks coverage or applicability. Display stale results with their original inputs and condition. Branch errors should identify the phase, property, file, or field that the user can address.

Determine ordinary calculation order from data wires and reject cycles. Keep sequential processing explicit in the schedule and state connections. Sweeps and optimizers can evaluate a bounded workflow repeatedly through their own scientific node.

## Phase resolution and branch coverage

**Resolve Phases** accepts a raw solver Phase Set or a manually supplied list of labels plus identification evidence. The Inspector shows original model, amount, composition, ordering evidence, assigned identity, available property coverage, and an **Include in this branch** checkbox per row. Prefer reviewed assessment rules and the exact-source inventory. Show provisional or competing matches with their evidence and let the user assign an applicable local record, CIF, Materials Project entry, or manually sourced data. A raw label such as `SIGMA_OLD` stays unresolved until evidence supports an assignment.

Keep the original immutable Phase Set, its TDB source key, and its phase amounts. Record filters and assignments against stable phase instance IDs. For `99.96 mol% FCC_A1 + 0.04 mol% AlCr`, a branch that excludes AlCr carries the original amounts and displays **99.96 mol% included · 0.04 mol% omitted**. The output of Density on this subset is labeled **FCC matrix only**. The full-alloy output requires full applicable volume coverage. Keep the underlying equilibrium solution and mobility model pinned through display edits, structural assignments, and branch selections.

Preserve the local MatCalc path through the graph. A source node supplies pinned assessment, mobility, and physical-data outputs. Existing MatCalc DP and Kawin operations can consume the original solver identity even when the canonical structure or MP reference is still unresolved. Save as much applicable property data as the user has, with an independent source and conditions for each property. The node catalog gives the per-file input rules and fallback order. [Phase registry](phase-registry.md) · [Current source handling](processing.md)

### Alloys outside the MatCalc presets

The current processing request uses the same `family` field for bundled
source selection, composition balance, and the dependent component in
equilibrium and Kawin. Even with a manual TDB selected, that field accepts only
Al, Fe, Mg, Mo, Ni, and Ti. The current graph also compares the composition base
to the selected preset before submitting. In an isolated code probe, relaxing
only the request's family type let the existing equilibrium engine use
`ReW-00Liu-LB.tdb` for W–10 at% Re at 101325 Pa. The engine found a liquid at
3900 K, completed the cooling path, and returned BCC_A2 at 2000 K within its
phase and elemental balance tolerances. This checks the execution path.
Experimental validation requires matched reference data. [Processing request](../backend/src/rutile3/domain/processing.py) · [Re–W assessment](../examples/README.md)

For a custom-alloy path, carry a `base_element` with the composition and let
the wired assessment or an optional MatCalc preset select the source. Validate
all selected elements against the assessment and retain evidence of interaction
coverage separately. Reuse the existing source hash, equilibrium solver, and
mass-balance checks. Add multiple independent addition rows to the Composition
node and use the assessment's declared elements for the picker. The current
processing API already supports up to eight additions. An arc-melt graph needs
a compatible liquid model and a reachable liquid temperature. A point or
solid-start graph would also support assessments intended for solid states.

For custom diffusion, use the actual selected solution phase and explicitly
paired mobility data. The current automatic phase filter and reference-phase
fallback are preset-specific. For density, evaluate any applicable physical
model or phase molar-volume references at the calculated phase compositions
and temperature. Missing companion files or incomplete property coverage
affect their branches while the equilibrium result remains available.
[Kawin adapter](../backend/src/rutile3/engines/processing.py) · [Density and source limits](processing.md)

## Saved workflows and reusable alloy data

Use a common `.rutile` extension for UTF-8 JSON documents with a published schema. Accept the same document with a `.json` extension through in-app import. Use `format: "rutile"` and `schema_version: 1` for the first schema, alongside `kind`, `document_id`, `name`, `created_at_utc`, `payload`, and `attachments`. Route imports by the validated header and schema. Define three initial document kinds.

| Kind | Required payload | Behavior on open or drop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workflow` | Node IDs and versioned operation IDs, settings, edges by node and pin ID, project-level inputs, and optional view state and saved result references. | Open the graph and show any missing source files or result artifacts. |
| `phase_set` | Conditions, phase instances, original fraction basis, assessment and model identity, selected or excluded instances, available property values, and provenance. | Create a Phase Set input node with a purple output. Values saved with the file can be inspected and reused offline. Recalculation asks for any missing original data source. |
| `material_state` | Composition, condition, phase set, chronological processing history, available microstructure, associated property results, and source references. Include a parent state ID when derived from another stage. | Create a Material State input node. The same object can feed a heat-treatment node, property branch, or visualization. |

Use immutable artifact IDs for the outputs referenced in a document. Keep provenance, basis, condition, and source checksums with saved values. Include parser and model versions in reproducible outputs. Large voxel maps, images, or raw engine results may use companion files identified by document-relative path, content type, byte size, and SHA-256. Offer a bundled export later when there are real large-data use cases. Use CIF for exchanging a known crystal structure and consider DREAM3D for exchanging spatial microstructure fields. Expose the applicable source terms when a file is included. [Core CIF dictionary](https://www.iucr.org/resources/cif/dictionaries/cif_core) · [DREAM3D file specification](https://www.dream3d.io/nx_reference_manual/html/Concepts/DREAM3DFileSpecification.html)

Show a preview of the imported type and any missing attachments. Resolve only permitted document-relative attachments or catalog items by checksum. Validate input size, structure, and schema version before storing it. Use atomic writes in the workspace. Associate `.rutile` through a small Windows launcher after import works. The launcher should start or reuse the loopback server and send the validated file through the same import path as a dropped file. Double-click opens the file or shows its typed input. Running a graph stays an explicit action. [Windows file type registration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/fa-file-types)

## Implementation boundaries

| Layer | Work |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend | Add a native JavaScript workspace under `frontend/src/js` and graph styles under `frontend/src/styles`. Reuse the shell, theme, motion settings, existing chart and result renderers, and browser accessibility conventions. Keep graph editing, drawing, and reading node results separate. |
| Domain | Define versioned Pydantic schemas for graph, pins, artifacts, states, and results. Publish one operation catalog with labels, stable IDs, versions, pin contracts, settings schema, and availability. Use it for editor compatibility and backend validation. |
| Services and API | Define a service that validates and schedules selected graph targets, resolves sources, and records graph revisions. Provide endpoints for catalog, graph validation, import, save/open, run, status, cancellation, and result retrieval. Keep I/O response schemas and HTTP error translation in `api/`. |
| Scientific adapters | Extract the selected-state equilibrium, property, and transport operations from the existing pipeline at the scientific boundary. Have both the graph and legacy processing route call those operations during migration. Keep each operation callable in tests and batch use without the UI. |
| Jobs and storage | Run CPU-bound nodes through the existing job manager and subprocess layer. Preserve process-tree cancellation, worker exit on coordinator loss, counted progress, source snapshots, and one native BLAS/OpenMP thread per process. Keep managed source imports and run outputs in the existing workspace storage layout. |

Build the cache key from operation and model versions, normalized scientific settings, input artifact hashes, and resolved source hashes. Pin an execution to a graph revision and its inputs. When an edit changes scientific inputs, mark affected descendants stale and keep the cached values available for inspection. Late results from an older revision attach to the submitted run. Write terminal results atomically before publishing completion. Resume a saved graph with completed results where their artifacts are available and start a new run for interrupted work. [Existing application architecture](architecture.md)

### Agent access

The Inspector is the first entry point. **Find reference** on a blocked pin gives the agent the phase instance, actual composition, applicable structure evidence, property, required units, and condition. Return candidate sources with record IDs or links, matching evidence, applicability limits, and reasons a candidate was rejected. Put any proposed assignment, conversion, or graph edit in a reviewable change. Use the same operation schemas and validation for UI and agent calls. A candidate can become a typed reference record when selected. Keep optional Materials Project credentials in the existing backend session path.

## Build order and acceptance

| Milestone | Deliverable | Acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Canvas and types | Main-menu entry, native editor, node catalog, graph save, and draft starter. | Keyboard and pointer can add, select, move, connect, and remove nodes. Dragging a Phase Set wire to empty space filters the menu and connects the chosen compatible pin. A Color → Image drop inserts Solid Fill. A Material Color → Image drop offers the three explicit conversions and identifies required data. At 390, 768, and 1440 CSS px, verify drawer access, no clipped controls, visible focus, and sharp settled rendering. |
| 2. Working equilibrium starter | Versioned graph runner, file/source nodes, equilibrium, phase inspection, and existing MatCalc density and tracer adapters. | Run the Al–Cu graph from pinned files with the Materials Project key absent. Verify phase and elemental balances, show coverage for incomplete density, and retrieve a completed result after reopening. Re-run Density after changing its reference and reuse equilibrium. Edit composition and show dependent results stale. Cancel a long job and retain earlier completed artifacts. |
| 3. Sharing and resolution | `.rutile` import/export, typed source nodes, phase assignment and filtering, and comparison summaries. | Export a Phase Set, open in a clean workspace, drop onto a canvas, and use it without rerunning equilibrium. Check omitted phase fractions, unresolved identities, duplicate phase names with different compositions, and a missing density reference. Verify unit conversion for equivalent values and a scoped check for an extreme strength result. |
| 4. Processed material states | Solidification, kinetics, and mechanistic property models added individually as applicable data become available. | Transfer from an explicitly selected starting state. Compare grain, precipitation, and property outputs with independent condition-matched benchmarks. Reopening a state preserves model parameters, evidence, and uncertainty. |
| 5. Appearance and design | Phase color, selected etch models, sweeps, and bounded optimization. | Reproduce benchmark reflectance-to-color conversions. Compare polished previews using supported phase data. Validate an etch model against measured relief for a matched bath, alloy, and exposure. Show which candidates are infeasible or unavailable in an optimization run. |

For the tracer node migration, add a regression where the cooling target and the final anneal or quench setpoint differ. Current Kawin processing reads composition from the final phase state and temperature from the original cooling target. The node must take both from its connected state. Test the explicit reference-only fallback independently from transport in a phase identified as present. For Density, check that a missing intermetallic volume preserves per-phase results and full-alloy coverage, and that omitting a trace phase produces a labeled subset result. [Current tracer implementation](../backend/src/rutile3/engines/processing.py) · [Density coverage methods](density-benchmarks.md)
# Development roadmap

The binary workflow now includes traced boundaries, phase-fraction gradients,
independent sample checks, Auto/Manual temperature ranges, live previews,
cancellation, inspection, and structured export. Windows sharing-lock handling
and targeted equilibrium retries are implemented. Synthetic scientific
regression tests and local Al–Cu, Ta–Zr, and Re–W browser checks cover numerical and
workflow behavior; published alloy benchmark validation remains outstanding.

The outlines below retain acceptance criteria for the broader project. They are
not all completed features. Material-point arc melting with equilibrium cooling and supplementary Kawin
tracer diffusion are implemented. Scheil solidification, precipitation kinetics,
calibrated property prediction, and optimization remain planned.
Alloy Studio can fit a preliminary flow law to a measured tensile curve.
The planned alloy-design workflow will calculate the flow curve from phase
states and processing-driven microstructure. It will use that curve to
predict yield, hardness, and UTS and account for fracture when it can limit
the tensile peak. [Mechanical properties](mechanical-properties.md)

The following are local issue outlines; no external issue tracker tickets have been created.

## 1. Database management foundation

Implementation detail: [Automatic TDB catalog and selection plan](database-selection-plan.md).

Deliver a catalog, configurable source registration, checksum-based duplicate detection, TDB parsing/validation, coverage inspection, and persistent source selection.

Acceptance:
- Register the existing database collection without editing source files.
- Distinguish thermodynamic, mobility, and volume capabilities.
- Given a requested system, explain suitable candidates and missing coverage.
- Save a selection with immutable source identity for reproducible runs.
- Report parsing failures without preventing valid files from being cataloged.

## 2. Binary phase diagram workflow

Deliver the first pycalphad adapter, explicit composition/units validation, calculation job lifecycle, structured results, plotting, and export.

Acceptance:
- Reproduce a documented reference binary diagram within stated tolerances.
- Keep numerical results and provenance independent of the displayed plot.
- Explain invalid inputs, unsupported systems, and failed calculations.
- Keep the UI responsive during a calculation and expose job status.

## 3. UI/UX foundation

The current interface has an animated intro, an interactive title screen, a tile menu, appearance settings, and the phase-diagram workspace. See the [interface guide](ui-ux.md) for screen behavior and styling.

Alloy Studio opens an editable Al–Cu starter graph with typed connections.
It runs equilibrium, local MatCalc density, and Kawin tracer diffusion in
separate jobs. The Project drawer provides workflow import and export and the
guided setup forms. Additional node types, portable phase and material states,
and optimization remain planned. [Workflow plan](alloy-studio-workflow-plan.md) · [Node catalog](alloy-studio-node-catalog.md)

Acceptance:
- A user can reach a diagram without manually choosing a TDB when a verified default is available.
- Ambiguous coverage prompts an understandable choice instead of silently selecting an arbitrary source.
- Forms are keyboard accessible and display units and composition basis.
- Loading, empty, success, and failure states are implemented.

## Later milestones

1. Curated property imports, phase-aware molar volume/density, and uncertainty metadata.
2. Scheil solidification and explicit transfer to processing simulations.
3. Processing models for grain size, precipitation, and other relevant microstructure variables, with compatible thermodynamic and mobility data and experimental validation.
4. A shared constitutive flow curve for yield, hardness, and the necking-controlled tensile peak. Use measured hardness as an optional constraint with independently established hardening. Couple a fracture or damage model when premature failure can limit the peak. Validate the individual stages and the full workflow with independent benchmarks.
5. Composition/process optimization with validity constraints and uncertainty-aware comparison.
6. Additional alloy families and optional ESPEI/matminer integrations.

"""Capture current UI with genuine completed runs for documentation.

Run against a local server with a --rew-job UUID. The authoring
browser redirects matching diagram submissions to those completed jobs to avoid
recalculating unchanged science. This is not an app cache or saved-run browser.
Numerical results are never synthesized or edited. Sources must match examples/.
"""
import argparse
from hashlib import sha256
from io import BytesIO
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image
from playwright.sync_api import expect, sync_playwright

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BASE = os.environ.get("RUTILE_TEST_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8000")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--rew-job', required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    output = ROOT / 'docs' / 'images'

    def capture(page, filename):
        page.mouse.move(5, 5)
        page.evaluate('document.fonts.ready')
        page.wait_for_timeout(150)
        screenshot = page.screenshot(full_page=True)
        with Image.open(BytesIO(screenshot)) as im:
            im.convert('RGB').save(output / filename, 'WEBP', quality=88, method=6)
        print(f'Captured {filename}', flush=True)

    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(channel='msedge', headless=True)
        context = browser.new_context(viewport={'width': 1500, 'height': 1040}, device_scale_factor=1)
        page = context.new_page()
        errors = []
        page.on('pageerror', lambda error: errors.append(str(error)))
        page.goto(BASE)
        page.locator('#title-heading').wait_for(state='visible')
        page.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        capture(page, 'title-screen.webp')
        page.locator('#title-settings').click()
        page.locator('#screen-settings').evaluate('el => Promise.all(el.getAnimations().map(a => a.finished))')
        page.wait_for_timeout(300)
        page.locator('#reduce-motion').check()
        page.locator('#shell-back').click()
        page.locator('#start-button').click()
        page.locator('#menu-optimize').click()
        page.locator('#studio-optimize').click()
        page.locator('#family-al').click()
        capture(page, 'alloy-family.webp')
        page.locator('#opt-next').click()
        for symbol, low, high in [('Mg', '.5', '1.5'), ('Si', '.4', '1')]:
            page.locator(f'[name="opt-element"][value="{symbol}"]').check()
            page.locator(f'#opt-{symbol}-min').fill(low)
            page.locator(f'#opt-{symbol}-max').fill(high)
        page.locator('#opt-next').click()
        page.locator('#opt-route').select_option('arc_melting')
        capture(page, 'alloy-processing.webp')
        page.locator('[data-opt-step="0"]').click()
        page.locator('#shell-back').click()  # Alloy Studio
        page.locator('#shell-back').click()  # Main menu
        page.locator('#menu-diagrams').click()
        for job, source, filename, x, temperature in [
            (args.rew_job, 'ReW-00Liu-LB.tdb', 're-w-phase-diagram.webp', .5, 2200),
        ]:
            response = page.request.get(f'{BASE}/api/jobs/{job}/result')
            assert response.ok, response.text()
            result = response.json()
            source_hash = sha256((ROOT / 'examples' / source).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            assert result['provenance']['sha256'] == source_hash
            settings = result['settings']
            page.locator('#upload').set_input_files(ROOT / 'examples' / source)
            page.wait_for_function("!document.querySelector('#calculate').disabled")
            page.locator('#calculation-settings').evaluate('el => el.open = true')
            mode = settings.get('temperature_mode', 'manual')
            page.locator('#temperature-mode').select_option(mode)
            if mode == 'manual':
                page.locator('#tmin').fill(str(settings['temperature_min']))
                page.locator('#tmax').fill(str(settings['temperature_max']))
            page.locator('#resolution').select_option(f"{settings['composition_points']},{settings['temperature_points']}")

            def replay(route):
                request = route.request.post_data_json
                assert request['database_id'] == source_hash
                keys = ['components', 'pressure', 'composition_points', 'temperature_points',
                        'boundary_steps', 'boundary_tolerance']
                if mode == 'manual':
                    keys += ['temperature_min', 'temperature_max']
                assert request['temperature_mode'] == mode
                for key in keys:
                    assert request[key] == settings[key], (key, request[key], settings[key])
                route.fulfill(status=202, json={'id': job})

            page.route('**/api/diagrams', replay)
            page.locator('#calculate').click()
            page.wait_for_function("document.querySelector('#workspace').dataset.stage === 'complete'")
            page.unroute('**/api/diagrams', replay)
            page.locator('#calculation-settings').evaluate('el => el.open = false')
            page.locator('#plot').scroll_into_view_if_needed()
            point = page.evaluate("""([x,t,low,high]) => {
                const plot=document.querySelector('#plot'), p=plot.createSVGPoint();
                p.x=76+x*670; p.y=25+465-(t-low)/(high-low)*465;
                const q=p.matrixTransform(plot.getScreenCTM());return {x:q.x,y:q.y};
            }""", [x, temperature, settings['temperature_min'], settings['temperature_max']])
            page.mouse.click(point['x'], point['y'])
            expect(page.locator('#unpin')).to_be_visible()
            page.evaluate('scrollTo(0,0)')
            capture(page, filename)
            print(json.dumps({'source': source, 'checks': result['validation']['counts'],
                              'composition_points': settings['composition_points'],
                              'temperature_points': settings['temperature_points']}), flush=True)
        assert not errors, errors
        browser.close()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
"""Real upload/worker/result/browser checks; local sources, no external network.

RUTILE_TEST_URL selects the running server. --matcalc also checks the
bundled family companions. Outputs stay in ignored workspace/.
"""
import argparse
import base64
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from time import monotonic, sleep

import requests
from playwright.sync_api import expect, sync_playwright

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BASE = os.environ.get("RUTILE_TEST_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8000")


def submit(payload):
    # A completed result can be published just before its worker exits. Wait for
    # that worker to retire before submitting the next calculation on this test server.
    for _ in range(50):
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE}/api/processing", json=payload, timeout=30)
        if response.status_code == 422 and response.json().get("detail") == "A calculation is already running. Wait or cancel it first.":
            sleep(.1)
            continue
        break
    assert response.status_code == 202, response.text
    response.raise_for_status()
    job = response.json()["id"]
    deadline = monotonic() + 240
    while monotonic() < deadline:
        status = requests.get(f"{BASE}/api/jobs/{job}", timeout=30).json()
        if status["state"] == "failed":
            raise AssertionError(status)
        if status["state"] == "completed":
            response = requests.get(f"{BASE}/api/jobs/{job}/result", timeout=30)
            response.raise_for_status()
            result = response.json()
            for state in result["states"]:
                assert abs(sum(p["fraction"] for p in state["phases"]) - 1) < 1e-5
                assert max(abs(error) for error in state["balance_errors"].values()) < 1e-5
            return job, result
        sleep(.4)
    requests.delete(f"{BASE}/api/jobs/{job}", timeout=30).raise_for_status()
    raise AssertionError("Processing worker exceeded workflow check timeout.")


def main(matcalc):
    output = ROOT / "workspace" / "processing-ui-check"
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    source = ROOT / "examples" / "AlCu-21Kro.tdb"
    response = requests.post(f"{BASE}/api/databases", json={"filename": source.name,
        "content": base64.b64encode(source.read_bytes()).decode(), "encoding": "base64"}, timeout=30)
    response.raise_for_status()
    key = response.json()["id"]
    payload = {"family": "AL", "database_id": key, "additions": [{"element": "CU", "maximum": 4}],
               "melt_temperature_k": 1073.15, "cooling_points": 5,
               "include_reference_properties": False}
    job, result = submit(payload)
    assert result["composition"]["nominal_percent"] == {"AL": 98, "CU": 2}
    assert result["kawin"]["state"] == "unavailable"  # No arbitrary companion pairing.
    (output / "uploaded-result.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"PASS upload, completed subprocess job and result retrieval: {job}", flush=True)
    # Start a real worker and cancel its process tree before its first solve.
    response = requests.post(f"{BASE}/api/processing", json={**payload, "cooling_points": 61}, timeout=30)
    response.raise_for_status()
    cancel_id = response.json()["id"]
    cancelled = requests.delete(f"{BASE}/api/jobs/{cancel_id}", timeout=30)
    cancelled.raise_for_status()
    assert cancelled.json()["state"] == "cancelled"
    assert requests.get(f"{BASE}/api/jobs/{cancel_id}/result", timeout=30).status_code == 409
    print("PASS real worker cancellation and incomplete-result protection", flush=True)
    if matcalc:
        manifest = json.loads((ROOT / 'data' / 'matcalc' / 'manifest.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
        cases = [
            ("AL", "CU", 1073.15), ("FE", "CR", 1973.15), ("NI", "CR", 1873.15),
            ("MG", "AL", 1073.15), ("TI", "AL", 2173.15), ("MO", "TI", 3173.15),
        ]

## Alloy Studio

Open **Alloy Studio** to edit the prewired Al–4 wt% Cu graph. Enter values
directly on **Composition** and **Processing Schedule**, or select a node to
edit its settings in the Inspector. Press Enter to commit a typed value.

![Alloy Studio starter showing editable fields on Composition and Processing Schedule, typed connections, and pinned MatCalc sources](docs/images/alloy-studio-workflow.webp)

Right-click the canvas to add a node. Drag an output into open space to search
for compatible nodes and wire in your selection. Right-click a wire to
disconnect it or double-click it to add a draggable reroute dot. Use
**Project** to open the starter, start a blank workflow, or import and export
`.rutile` files.

Use **Run Graph** to calculate equilibrium and run the connected branches.
Use a node's play button to run its branch with the current equilibrium
result. **Phase Viewer** shows phase amounts in mol% and compositions in at%.
**Density** reports per-phase coverage, and **Tracer Diffusivity** identifies
the evaluated phase and temperature.

![Completed Al–Cu workflow at 800 K with a MatCalc density estimate and a labeled parent-phase approximation in the Inspector](docs/images/alloy-studio-density.webp)

For the run shown above, the cooling target was set to **800 K** and
**Allow disordered parent density** was enabled on Density. The Inspector
labels the linked-parent approximation and shows the coverage for that run.
[Canvas controls](docs/ui-ux.md#alloy-studio-workflows) · [Processing methods](docs/processing.md)

### Bundled databases

The repository includes Al, Fe, Mg, Mo, Ni, and Ti MatCalc thermodynamic assessments,
their matching mobility files, and the physical density database under
`data/matcalc/`. The family source and mobility companion are ready when the app
starts. The bundle retains the original files and their checksums. [Source attribution and licenses](data/matcalc/README.md)

To use a different assessment, add a **Thermodynamic File** node and wire it into
MatCalc Sources. **Mobility File** and **Physical Data File** accept explicit
companions. Tracer calculations with a manual assessment require a compatible
mobility file. Set `RUTILE_DATABASE_ROOT` to replace the default source
collection or `RUTILE_PHYSICAL_DATABASE` to select another local density file.

## Materials Project property references

Open **Settings → Materials Project**, enter your API key, and choose **Save key**.
The server holds the key in memory until restart. **Clear session key** removes
it and restores any environment key. To configure a persistent key, copy
[.env.example](.env.example) to a local `.env` file, set `MP_API_KEY`, and restart
Rutile. The standard launcher loads the file and respects an existing environment
value.

## Alloy Studio workflows

The first visit opens **Al–Cu equilibrium**. Drag a header to move a node and
drag empty canvas to pan. Scroll or use the zoom buttons to zoom. **Fit graph**
fits the current layout. Right-click or press Enter on the focused canvas to
open Add Node. Type to filter and use arrow keys and Enter to choose a result.
Dragging an output into empty space filters the same menu by pin type and
connects the new node at the release point or the closest open position.
Right-click a wire to disconnect it. Double-click a wire to add a reroute dot,
then drag the dot or use the arrow keys when it is focused. Right-click a dot
or press Delete on it to remove that point. Routes are saved with the graph.
With a keyboard, activate an output, then activate the
receiving input or open Add Node. The Inspector lists connections and offers
disconnect and remove actions.

In the starter, Composition supplies one addition with an explicit mass or
atomic basis and a base-element balance. Processing Schedule supplies the
initial, melt, and cooling target temperatures, cooling points, and pressure.
Edit these values directly on the nodes or in the Inspector. Enter commits a
typed value. Both views reflect the same settings and the composition balance
updates on commit.
For a custom file, add and select a **Thermodynamic File**, **Mobility File**,
or **Physical Data File** node, choose a file, and wire it to the corresponding
MatCalc Sources input. Density and Tracer Diffusivity also accept their
respective file outputs directly.

**Run Graph** runs the connected calculation nodes in dependency order. Each
play button runs its branch and any stale prerequisite. Editing scientific
inputs marks old results stale. Changing Density's reference option keeps the
equilibrium result current. Select Phase Viewer for the final phase table or a
calculation node for its result and JSON export. Density reports missing
coverage, including per-phase reasons. The Inspector can enable the existing
linked disordered-parent density approximation and labels the affected phases.
Tracer results show the selected phase,
temperature, pressure, and coefficients in m²/s.

The browser restores the last graph and available completed runs from this app
address. **Project → Export workflow** saves a portable graph definition.
Reopen it from Project or drop it onto the canvas. Use the same catalog or
reselect custom source files on another installation. The Inspector stacks
below the graph on narrow screens. The app's reduced-motion setting applies to
the transitions.

**Project → Guided setup** retains the composition forms and advanced thermal
events for Create Alloy and Optimize Alloy. The graph starter exposes arc-melt
equilibrium, density, and tracer diffusivity. Additional processing and property
nodes are described in the [node catalog](alloy-studio-node-catalog.md).

## Mechanical properties

The tensile-analysis API accepts a CSV or TSV upload or a locally available reference test. The analysis displays
proof stress, the measured peak and fitted flow curve where available, with
keyboard and pointer inspection and JSON export. The **Estimate strength from
composition** prototype is unsuitable for new-alloy design. The planned
mechanistic workflow uses calculated microstructure as its input.
[Mechanical properties and model requirements](mechanical-properties.md)
# Rutile3 development instructions

## Purpose and priorities

Develop the local materials modeling application to design new alloys. Use CALPHAD phase identities, compositions, and amounts with processing history to calculate the microstructure and predict properties with mechanistic models. The equilibrium foundation currently uses a FastAPI/Python backend, pycalphad solver, and HTML/CSS/native JavaScript UI. Implemented features include thermodynamic database inspection and import, binary equilibrium phase maps at fixed pressure, Auto/Manual temperature limits, parallel CPU workers, live previews and counted progress, cancellation, point inspection, JSON export, and optional Materials Project reference lookups.

Alloy Studio supports material-point equilibrium through melting and cooling, compatible tracer diffusion, density and elasticity estimates, and measured tensile-curve analysis. Mechanistic property prediction, solidification kinetics, precipitation, and alloy optimization remain planned. Published alloy benchmark validation is also outstanding. Numerical regression tests use synthetic regular-solution, ideal-melting, and order/disorder models. See `README.md` for usage, `docs/roadmap.md` before expanding scope, and `docs/phase-diagrams.md` for binary methods and limits.

This is a class final project and a personal project. The user's hands-on experience is with cast Al–Cu and Zn alloys, and the goal is a genuinely useful materials-science application that feels good to use, not just a working prototype. The work is taxing, especially data acquisition: the UI, property-modeling math, and scientific work are interesting, but hunting down sources (for example, an old study of copper's Young's modulus that stops applying once manganese is added) is the main pain point. Reduce the user's burden on data acquisition and literature searches, and keep the application itself pleasant to use.

## Communication and responses

- Be goal- and results-oriented: lead with what the user needs to do next and the implications of findings, not a wall of text.
- Keep answers easy and straightforward: short, direct, and structured where it helps. No filler, no restated context.
- The standard is that the agent does its job so the user can do theirs. Minimize the user's effort, especially on data acquisition and literature searches: surface what is needed, where it comes from, and why a candidate source may not apply.

## Environment and layout

- Use Python 3.12 in the project virtual environment. Run `.venv/Scripts/python.exe` on Windows and `.venv/bin/python` on other platforms, from the repository root.
- Install with `python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'` using that environment's interpreter. On Windows, also pass `-c requirements-win-py312.txt`; these constraints are specific to Windows/Python 3.12.
- Start with the environment's Python and `scripts/run_app.py` (optional `--open` or `--port 8001`). It serves the API and frontend on loopback, port 8000 by default. The frontend has no Node.js dependency or build step.
- Backend source belongs in `backend/src/rutile3`; frontend source belongs in `frontend/src`.
- Declare dependencies in the root `pyproject.toml`; install into the project environment, not the system interpreter.
- Keep documentation under `docs/` and update it when behavior or architectural decisions change.
- Preserve the native JavaScript modules. Do not introduce a frontend framework or build system without a concrete feature need.
- Use the existing checkout in an isolated cloud task; do not create a Git worktree unless explicitly requested. Keep machine-specific setup and credentials out of these shared instructions.

I’d prioritize **wire snapping, node deletion, and a clearly runnable starter**, then bring the wizard’s thermal editor into the graph. I reviewed the current code and checked-in screenshot. Live browser verification was blocked by local socket permissions. This was a review only.

1. **Make wires snap to compatible inputs.** Today the preview follows the cursor and checks the destination on release. Highlight compatible pins as soon as the drag begins, then snap the preview to the nearest valid pin within a forgiving drop radius. If that input already has a wire, show that dropping will replace it. Use the same highlights when connecting by keyboard. [Wire handling](/Y:/Rutile3/frontend/src/js/alloy-studio.js:718)

2. **Make nodes removable directly on the canvas.** The Inspector already has **Remove node**. Give selected nodes a visible **×** and support **Delete** and **Backspace** when focus is on the canvas or node. Keep those keys editing text inside fields. Add Undo so a deletion can restore the node and its wires. [Existing removal action](/Y:/Rutile3/frontend/src/js/alloy-studio.js:583)

3. **Show that the starter’s inputs are configured.** The Al–4 wt% Cu starter already ships with composition, a thermal schedule, and eight wires. The empty file pins on MatCalc Al are optional overrides, but the canvas gives them the same appearance as disconnected inputs. Show the resolved thermodynamic, mobility, and physical data sources on the node, put overrides behind an expansion control, and flag genuinely missing inputs by name before Run. Verify the starter from a fresh session without a Materials Project key, with any unavailable density clearly attributed to phase coverage. [Starter graph](/Y:/Rutile3/frontend/src/js/alloy-graph.js:35) · [Current input status](/Y:/Rutile3/frontend/src/js/alloy-studio.js:177)

4. **Reuse the wizard’s thermal graph in Processing Schedule.** Put a compact temperature preview on the node and the full chart and event editor in the Inspector. Carry over temperature changes, anneals, and quenches, and persist those events with the workflow so they reach the solver. The chart should retain its event-sequence axis and identify hold times and quench media as recorded conditions. [Wizard editor](/Y:/Rutile3/frontend/src/js/processing-events.js:41) · [Current graph request](/Y:/Rutile3/frontend/src/js/alloy-runs.js:23)

The next gap I’d close is **phase inspection along the schedule**. Phase Viewer shows only the final state today. ## Alloy Studio graph

Native editor modules in `frontend/src/js/alloy-*.js` validate typed
connections and select runnable targets. Browser storage keeps graph settings
and references to completed local job IDs. The editor compares calculation
inputs to choose current results or mark descendants stale. The backend
validates scientific inputs independently. Graph equilibrium jobs snapshot the
assessment and its default companions. Density and tracer branch jobs derive
their input from the completed server-side equilibrium artifact and retain
their own source snapshots. Imported companion files live under
`workspace/imports/workflow/` by role and checksum.
[Workflow controls](ui-ux.md#alloy-studio-workflows)

## Mechanical calculations

The tensile workflow snapshots the uploaded or selected reference trace and runs
through the subprocess job layer. `data/tensile.py` reads engineering strain and
stress, `services/mechanical.py` manages the job inputs and provenance, and
`properties/mechanical.py` derives proof stress and fits the uniform plastic
portion of the trace. See [tensile analysis](mechanical-properties.md#analyze-a-tensile-trace).

"""Material-point processing schedules and equilibrium inputs."""
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator

from rutile3.domain.selection import Element


class AdditionBound(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False)
    element: Element
    minimum: float = Field(default=0, ge=0, lt=100)
    maximum: float = Field(gt=0, lt=100)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_bounds(self):
        self.element = self.element.upper()
        if self.minimum > self.maximum:
            raise ValueError("Minimum addition must not exceed maximum.")
        return self


class ProcessingEvent(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False)


class TemperatureChange(ProcessingEvent):
    kind: Literal["temperature_change"]
    temperature_k: float = Field(ge=273.15, le=4000)
    duration_s: float | None = Field(default=None, gt=0)


class Anneal(ProcessingEvent):
    kind: Literal["anneal"]
    temperature_k: float = Field(ge=273.15, le=2500)
    hold_s: float = Field(gt=0)


class Quench(ProcessingEvent):
    kind: Literal["quench"]
    medium: Literal["water", "oil", "air", "brine"]
    temperature_k: float = Field(ge=273.15, le=2500)


class ColdWork(ProcessingEvent):
    kind: Literal["cold_work"]
    reduction_pct: float = Field(gt=0, lt=100)


ScheduleEvent = Annotated[TemperatureChange | Anneal | Quench | ColdWork, Field(discriminator="kind")]


class ProcessingRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False)
    family: Literal["AL", "FE", "NI", "MG", "TI", "MO"]
    database_id: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=64)
    composition_basis: Literal["mass", "atomic"] = "mass"
    composition_mode: Literal["bounds", "fixed"] = "bounds"
    additions: list[AdditionBound] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=8)
    route: Literal["arc_melting", "heat_treatment"] = "arc_melting"
    cooling_model: Literal["equilibrium"] = "equilibrium"
    phase_policy: Literal["all_compatible", "fe_cementite"] = "all_compatible"
    initial_temperature_k: float = Field(default=298.15, ge=273.15, le=2500)
    melt_temperature_k: float = Field(default=1873.15, ge=273.15, le=4000)
    final_temperature_k: float = Field(default=298.15, ge=273.15, le=2500)
    pressure_pa: float = Field(default=101325, gt=0, le=1e9)
    cooling_points: int = Field(default=21, ge=3, le=61)
    events: list[ScheduleEvent] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=24)
    notes: str = Field(default="", max_length=2000)
    include_reference_properties: bool = True
    allow_screening_estimates: bool = True
    use_physical_density: bool = True

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_cycle(self):
        elements = [bound.element for bound in self.additions]
        if len(elements) != len(set(elements)) or self.family in elements:
            raise ValueError("Choose distinct additions and exclude the base element.")
        if self.phase_policy == "fe_cementite" and (self.family != "FE" or elements != ["C"]):
            raise ValueError("Fe–Fe₃C equilibrium requires iron with carbon as its sole addition.")
        if sum(bound.maximum for bound in self.additions) >= 100:
            raise ValueError("Maximum additions must leave a positive base balance.")
        if self.composition_mode == "fixed" and any(bound.minimum != bound.maximum for bound in self.additions):
            raise ValueError("Fixed composition requires equal minimum and maximum amounts.")
        if self.route == "arc_melting" and self.melt_temperature_k <= max(self.initial_temperature_k, self.final_temperature_k):
            raise ValueError("The melt temperature must exceed initial and final temperatures.")
        if self.route == "heat_treatment" and not self.events:
            raise ValueError("Add a processing event for heat treatment or cold work.")
        temperature = self.final_temperature_k if self.route == "arc_melting" else self.initial_temperature_k
        for index, event in enumerate(self.events):
            if isinstance(event, ColdWork):
                if index != len(self.events) - 1:
                    raise ValueError("Cold work must be the last processing event.")
                continue
            if isinstance(event, Quench) and event.temperature_k >= temperature:
                raise ValueError("The quench temperature must be below the preceding temperature.")
            temperature = event.temperature_k
        return self

    def nominal_percent(self):
        values = {bound.element: bound.maximum * (1 if self.composition_mode == "fixed" else .5) for bound in self.additions}
        return {self.family: 100 - sum(values.values()), **values}

const script = String.raw`import contextlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import requests
from playwright.sync_api import expect, sync_playwright

ROOT = Path.cwd()
RUN_ROOT = ROOT / "workspace" / "studio-edit-verification"
URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8766"

def graph(page):
    return page.evaluate("JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('rutile.alloy-studio.v1')).graph")

def enter(page):
    page.goto(URL, timeout=45000)
    page.locator("#start-button").click(timeout=25000)
    page.locator("#menu-optimize").click()
    expect(page.locator(".studio-viewport")).to_be_visible()
    page.locator('[data-action="fit"]').click()
    expect(page.locator('[data-node="sources"] [data-role="assessment"] dd')).to_have_text("mc_al_v2037.tdb")

def run_graph(page):
    with page.expect_response(lambda response: response.url.endswith("/api/workflow/equilibrium"), timeout=20000) as sent:
        page.locator('[data-action="run"]').click()
    assert sent.value.status == 202, sent.value.text()
    job = sent.value.json()["id"]
    expect(page.locator('[data-action="run"]')).to_be_enabled(timeout=180000)
    failures = page.locator('.studio-node-note[data-status="failed"]').all_text_contents()
    assert not failures, failures
    result = page.request.get(f"{URL}/api/jobs/{job}/result")
    assert result.ok, result.text()
    return sent.value.request.post_data_json, result.json()

def check(page, browser):
    page.set_default_timeout(12000)
    errors = []
    page.on("pageerror", lambda error: errors.append(str(error)))
    enter(page)
    expect(page.locator('.studio-node')).to_have_count(7)
    sources = page.locator('[data-node="sources"]')
    expect(sources.locator(".studio-title")).to_have_text("Data Sources")
    expect(sources.locator('[data-role="mobility"] dd')).to_have_text("mc_al_v2008.ddb")
    expect(sources.locator('[data-role="physical"] dd')).to_have_text("physical_data.pdb")
    overrides = sources.locator("[data-overrides]")
    expect(sources.locator('[data-direction="input"]:visible')).to_have_count(0)
    overrides.click()
    expect(sources.locator('[data-direction="input"]:visible')).to_have_count(3)
    overrides.click()
    page.locator('[data-node="composition"] [data-title]').click()
    element = page.locator('[data-node="composition"] [data-field="element"]')
    element.focus()
    element.press("Backspace")
    element.fill("CU")
    element.press("Enter")
    expect(page.locator(".studio-node")).to_have_count(7)
    page.locator('[data-node="schedule"] [data-title]').click()
    page.keyboard.press("x")
    expect(page.locator('[data-node="schedule"]')).to_have_count(0)
    expect(page.locator('[data-node="equilibrium"] .studio-node-note')).to_contain_text("Connect Processing Schedule")
    page.keyboard.press("Control+z")
    expect(page.locator('[data-node="schedule"]')).to_have_count(1)
    assert len(graph(page)["edges"]) == 8
    page.locator('[data-node="viewer"] [data-title]').click()
    page.keyboard.press("Delete")
    expect(page.locator('[data-node="viewer"]')).to_have_count(0)
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Undo removal").click()
    expect(page.locator('[data-node="viewer"]')).to_have_count(1)

    page.locator('[data-action="add"]').click()
    page.locator('.studio-library [data-add="composition"]').click()
    extra = next(n["id"] for n in graph(page)["nodes"] if n["type"] == "composition" and n["id"] != "composition")
    page.locator('[data-action="fit"]').click()
    source = page.locator(f'[data-node="{extra}"] [data-direction="output"]')
    compatible = page.locator('[data-node="equilibrium"] [data-pin="composition"]')
    incompatible = page.locator('[data-node="equilibrium"] [data-pin="assessment"]')
    def center(locator):
        box = locator.locator('i').bounding_box()
        return (box["x"] + box["width"] / 2, box["y"] + box["height"] / 2)
    x, y = center(source)
    target_x, target_y = center(compatible)
    page.mouse.move(x - 2, y)
    page.mouse.down()
    page.mouse.move(target_x - 12, target_y, steps=12)
    expect(compatible).to_have_class(re.compile(r"\bcompatible\b"))
    expect(compatible).to_have_class(re.compile(r"\bsnapped\b"))
    expect(incompatible).not_to_have_class(re.compile(r"\bcompatible\b"))
    expect(page.locator('.studio-wire.pending.snapped')).to_have_count(1)
    expect(page.locator('.studio-status output')).to_have_text("Replace Composition")
    page.mouse.up()
    expect(page.locator('.studio-wire.pending')).to_have_count(0)
    assert [extra, "composition", "equilibrium", "composition"] in graph(page)["edges"]
    page.locator('[data-node="composition"] [data-direction="output"]').press("Enter")
    expect(compatible).to_have_class(re.compile(r"\bcompatible\b"))
    compatible.press("Enter")
    assert ["composition", "composition", "equilibrium", "composition"] in graph(page)["edges"]
    page.locator(f'[data-node="{extra}"] [data-title]').click()
    page.keyboard.press("Backspace")
    page.locator('[data-action="fit"]').click()
    print("PASS default sources, draft input warning, keyboard deletion and undo, pointer snap and keyboard connect", flush=True)

    first, reference = run_graph(page)
    assert first["route"] == "arc_melting" and first["cooling_points"] == 21
    assert reference["composition"]["nominal_percent"] == {"AL": 96.0, "CU": 4.0}
    assert reference["provenance"]["source_name"] == "mc_al_v2037.tdb"
    print("PASS fresh starter completed equilibrium, density, and tracer jobs without a Materials Project key", flush=True)
    page.locator('[data-node="schedule"] [data-edit-schedule]').click()
    expect(page.locator("#studio-thermal-plot .thermal-line")).to_have_count(2)
    editor = page.locator(".studio-schedule-editor")
    editor.locator('[data-field="points"]').fill("3")
    editor.locator('[data-field="points"]').press("Enter")
    menu = editor.locator('#studio-process-add')
    menu.locator(':scope > summary').click()
    menu.locator('[data-add-event="anneal"]').click()
    first_event = editor.locator('[data-kind="anneal"]')
    expect(page.locator('[data-node="equilibrium"] .studio-node-note')).to_contain_text("Event 1")
    first_event.locator('.event-temperature').fill("400")
    first_event.locator('.event-duration').fill("15")
    menu.locator(':scope > summary').click()
    menu.locator('.process-menu details > summary').click()
    menu.locator('[data-medium="water"]').click()
    expect(page.locator("#studio-thermal-plot .hold")).to_have_count(1)
    expect(page.locator("#studio-thermal-plot .quench")).to_have_count(1)
    expect(page.locator('[data-node="schedule"] svg .hold')).to_have_count(1)
    page.reload()
    page.locator("#start-button").click()
    page.locator("#menu-optimize").click()
    page.locator('[data-action="fit"]').click()
    page.locator('[data-node="schedule"] [data-edit-schedule]').click()
    expect(first_event.locator("summary")).to_contain_text("15 min hold")
    expect(editor.locator('[data-kind="quench"] summary')).to_contain_text("Water quench")
    submitted, executed = run_graph(page)
    assert submitted["events"] == [
        {"kind": "anneal", "temperature_k": 673.15, "hold_s": 900},
        {"kind": "quench", "temperature_k": 298.15, "medium": "water"},
    ], submitted
    assert executed["final"]["temperature_k"] == 298.15
    assert executed["settings"]["events"] == submitted["events"]
    assert all(abs(sum(phase["fraction"] for phase in state["phases"]) - 1) < 1e-5 for state in executed["states"])
    assert not errors, errors
    print("PASS shared schedule editor, reload, equilibrium setpoints, and serialized thermal events", flush=True)

    mobile = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 390, "height": 844}, device_scale_factor=2, has_touch=True, is_mobile=True, reduced_motion="reduce")
    enter(mobile)
    mobile.locator('[data-node="schedule"] [data-edit-schedule]').tap()
    visible = mobile.locator("#studio-thermal-plot")
    expect(visible).to_be_visible()
    assert mobile.locator(".studio-inspector").evaluate("element => element.scrollWidth <= element.clientWidth + 1")
    mobile.locator("#studio-process-add > summary").tap()
    mobile.locator('#studio-process-add [data-add-event="temperature_change"]').tap()
    expect(mobile.locator('#studio-process-events [data-kind="temperature_change"]')).to_have_count(1)
    mobile.close()
    print("PASS mobile inspector layout and touch controls at 390 CSS pixels", flush=True)

    page.locator('[data-action="project"]').click()
    page.locator('.studio-project details > summary').click()
    page.locator('.studio-project [data-alloy-mode="create"]').click()
    page.locator("#family-al").click()
    page.locator("#opt-next").click()
    page.locator('[name="opt-element"][value="Cu"]').check()
    page.locator('#opt-Cu-amount').fill('4')
    page.locator("#opt-next").click()
    expect(page.locator("#thermal-plot .thermal-line")).to_have_count(2)
    page.locator("#process-add > summary").click()
    page.locator('#process-add [data-add-event="anneal"]').click()
    page.locator('#process-events .event-temperature').fill('400')
    page.locator('#process-events .event-duration').fill('15')
    expect(page.locator("#thermal-plot .hold")).to_have_count(1)
    assert not errors, errors
    print("PASS legacy wizard still edits and renders the same anneal schedule", flush=True)

def main():
    RUN_ROOT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    env = dict(os.environ)
    for key in ("MP_API_KEY", "RUTILE_DATABASE_ROOT", "RUTILE_PHYSICAL_DATABASE"):
        env.pop(key, None)
    env.update(RUTILE_WORKSPACE=str(RUN_ROOT), RUTILE_CATALOG_PATH=str(RUN_ROOT / "catalog.sqlite3"))
    with (RUN_ROOT / "server.log").open("w", encoding="utf-8") as log:
        server = subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, "-u", "-m", "uvicorn", "rutile3.api.app:app", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "8766"],
            cwd=ROOT, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW,
        )
        try:
            deadline = time.monotonic() + 90
            while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                if server.poll() is not None:
                    raise RuntimeError((RUN_ROOT / "server.log").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                try:
                    if requests.get(URL, timeout=3).ok:
                        break
                except requests.ConnectionError:
                    pass
                time.sleep(.5)
            else:
                raise RuntimeError("Local server did not start.")
            with sync_playwright() as p:
                browser = p.chromium.launch(channel="msedge", headless=True, timeout=45000)
                page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1440, "height": 960}, reduced_motion="reduce")
                check(page, browser)
        finally:
            with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
                server.terminate()
            server.wait(timeout=15)

if __name__ == "__main__":

# Alloy processing methods

The Alloy Studio starter graph runs equilibrium, density, and tracer diffusivity
through separate subprocess jobs. The two property branches read the completed
equilibrium artifact and pinned assessment. Explicit file nodes can supply
companion files for those branches. Use **Project → Guided setup** for the
advanced schedule and plain-carbon steel controls described below.

Alloy Studio calculates the equilibrium of a homogeneous material point at fixed
pressure. The starting route can include an arc melt and sampled equilibrium
cooling, or start with a solid alloy. The solver verifies a fully liquid melt
for the arc-melting route. Results report phase amounts on a molar basis and
phase compositions on an atomic basis. [Alloy studio walkthrough](../README.md#alloy-studio)

The ordered schedule supports temperature changes, anneals, quenches, and a
final cold-work thickness reduction. The editor uses °C and minutes. API inputs
use K and seconds. The temperature chart shows event order, with no time scale.
The job preserves settings for every event and calculates an independent
equilibrium at each thermal setpoint. The quenched result is the equilibrium
at the target temperature. The entered duration, hold time, quench medium, and
cold-work reduction are preserved for future kinetic and deformation models.
Cold work adds no equilibrium solve. Segregation, precipitation, quench
transformations, and grain evolution remain model gaps.

An automatic anneal could first screen the temperature interval for the
specified phase objective and incipient melting using the selected assessment.
Selecting a temperature and hold time for a target such as recrystallized
fraction or grain size requires the starting condition, kinetic parameters,
and a validated model. The Anneal event uses a user-entered setpoint and hold.
[Equilibrium phase fractions](https://pycalphad.org/docs/latest/examples/2_Computing_Properties/1_PhaseCompositions.html)
· [Recrystallization modeling](https://www.matcalc.at/images/stories/publications/phd_thesis_buken_2018.pdf)

Create alloy submits fixed additions in wt% or at%. Optimize alloy uses half
of each addition's maximum for the nominal phase simulation. The base fills the
balance. The saved `composition_mode` identifies the rule. A fixed request
supplies equal minimum and maximum values for each addition.

The default source root contains the named Al, Fe, Mg, Mo, Ni, and Ti MatCalc thermodynamic
and mobility pairs. The worker snapshots the original TDB and mobility data,
records checksums and solver versions, and writes a separate converted TDB for
pycalphad. Manual thermodynamic sources retain their own models. Kawin evaluates
tracer diffusivities where the paired mobility source and the selected phase
model are compatible. [Bundled databases and source terms](../data/matcalc/README.md)

## Plain-carbon steel equilibrium

content.text:
Implemented all four Alloy Studio changes.

- **Wire snapping.** Compatible inputs light up while you drag. The wire snaps to a nearby pin and shows **Replace** if dropping will overwrite an existing connection.
- **Keyboard deletion.** Select a node and press **X**, **Delete**, or **Backspace**. **Ctrl+Z** or **Undo removal** restores the node and its wires before the next graph edit. Text fields keep their normal shortcuts.
- **Generic Data Sources.** The Al–Cu starter preselects the MatCalc Al assessment, its mobility companion, and the physical data file. Missing required inputs are flagged before a run.
- **Thermal schedule.** Processing Schedule shows a compact preview and opens the wizard’s full chart and event editor in the Inspector. Events are saved with the workflow and passed to the solver, which calculates equilibrium at each thermal setpoint.

All **122 tests passed**. Edge verification covered desktop and mobile controls, the starter without a Materials Project key, an uploaded assessment override, and a saved anneal and quench workflow.
